TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_001: Attendees love our fins-on activities. Just look at that one over there, who seems most loath to let go of his horse! But we cannot afford to rest in our jars just yet. You see, our dramatic demise, our painful annihila─ Oh, I forgot to call Gyorei and Gyofun. One moment, please.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_002: I have summoned you all here for one reason. Yes, ye─
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: I assume this will again be some nonsense about dreams and prophecies? You must recall that I cautioned you against eating unidentified plant matter.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_004: If it comes from the ground, it is food! Yes, yes. Just because I was rendered violently ill, incapacitated for a fortnight by those green mushrooms does not mean... Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, yes, yes. I have continued to see our greatest grandsire in my dreams.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: ...Though the dreams of your addled mind are immaterial to my goal of enlightening one and all, I have identified an aspect in which our festival is lacking compared to those of our ancestors.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_006: That is fantastic, Seigetsu the Enlightened. Yes, yes. Though I cannot help but worry that you are about to─
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Allow me to elaborate in detail! Culture is an ever-evolving beast, you see. The radicalization of culture, in particular, results in unique cultural expressions that outsiders struggle to comprehend. When it is applied to ritual, festivals become true carnivals of the bizarre.

Given that our ancestors' festivals were known as “unforgettable spectacles,” should we not assume they had a fair few radical elements? In which case, our event must needs include at least one uniquely memorable ritual if we are to carry on their legacy.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_009: That actually sounds interesting! I am most intrigued. What happens in these rituals that everyone finds so strange?
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: I haven't the foggiest! Religious rituals are secretive by nature, my dear Gyoshin!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_011: Perhaps it is my own fault. Yes, yes. I neglected to remember Gyofun's unhelpfulness. I suppose we will put this matter to rest for now. Call it a day.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Now, hold on a moment! Your lack of intellectual curiosity is no fault of mine. The correct response would be to acknowledge our need to engage in further research.
Occidentalism makes mention of a Sharlayan society devoted to the pursuit of knowledge. One of their number might be privy to the information we seek.

One such as yourself must know Sharlayans of the intellectual persuasion we require. Preferably someone wizened. With arcane knowledge. Who is also an expert in rituals. Surely you know a few fitting that profile?
Master Matoya in Dravania, you say? Yes, she sounds ideal. It is so convenient that you foreigners all know each other.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_016: Yes, yes. She sounds most convenient. Much more useful than Gyofun.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_017: I hate─really hate─to ask, but could you convey me to Master Matoya's in your bag?
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOREI_000_025: I realize that looking after Gyoshin can be exhausting. Yes, yes. In a variety of ways.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_030: ...I don't suppose you've a reason for lugging that thing around?
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_040: Is this the place? Please tell me this is the place.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_041: Hello, hello! Are you Master Matoya? I am relieved to see you so moist, so slimy. From 's description, you sounded most dry and intimidating!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_042: Eager to get off on the wrong foot, aren't we?
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_043: ...Oh. Oh no. The scary lady is Master Matoya?
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_044: I am so sorry. Most apologetic! I was confused.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_045: Well, since you and your bumbling companion have already disrupted my routine, I suppose I'll hear you out. I presume you've a reason for coming here other than to annoy me?
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_046: Oh, the world is hardly short on carnivals of the bizarre.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_047: Competitive cheese-rolling, fertility rituals where the bride gets whacked with a stick─I tell you if someone tried that with me, they'd be out an eye─whatever nonsense you can imagine, someone's getting up to it.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_048: But if you seek to avert a calamitous fate, I trust you'll want to do better than those half-baked traditions.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_049: For a truly memorable spectacle, you'll want to revive a ceremony so terrible, so horrible that few would dare to even whisper of it. One so steeped in evil that men swore never again to perform it!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_050: Oooh, evil! Darkness! Tell me more! Tell me more!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_051: If you shrink not from these horrors, I assume you are prepared to not only sully your hands, but your very soul.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_052: Yes, yes! I will save the Namazu, even if I must endure a never-ending celebration. Even if I must work my fins to the bone.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_053: Color me impressed. Confused, but impressed.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_054: I'll prepare a simple manuscript on forbidden rituals for you. Just stay put. Have some tea. Do whatever it is you Namazu do.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_055: Here we are. Only three hundred pages, but it should serve.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_057: Ah, right. Tea makes Namazu tipsy. Lucky you.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_058: It's a miracle they've survived this long. Well, back in the sack with him!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_MATOYA_000_060: Had anyone else shown up on my doorstep with a Namazu in tow, I would've had my poroggos deal with them. I'm still not quite sure what you're about, but if it gets you to stop fighting every other god or dragon for a spell, it can't be all that bad.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_071: ...Fresh air at last. <groan> You might want to wash that. It smells like vomit in there.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_072: A-Anyway, we should focus on this tome Matoya so kindly, most generously gave us.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: A manuscript penned by the Sharlayan scholar herself? I must peruse it without delay!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_074: Yes, yes. It is most illuminating. So full of information on fascinating rituals that I can hardly decide which we should attempt!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Relinquish that this instant! I must read it!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_076: Just a moment, please, please. This one is just so... Oh, but this one is also...
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Give it here, I say. Now. NOW!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_083: Yes, yes! There can be only one! No other!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_084: This “Wicker Man” is the perfect choice. We must incinerate a live sacrifice inside a massive effigy!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_085: It is the only way to avert total Namazu annihilation! Yes...yes...
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: I...daresay he ought to be stopped, but it may be unwise to anger him just now.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_100: To work! We require a large Namazu effigy. You must help me build it. You will not defy me, no, no?
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_101: You will find materials to create a metal clamp in the crate. I expect you to bring me the finest you have ever made, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_102: You will find materials to create papier-mache in the crate. I expect you to bring me the finest you have ever made, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_103: You will find materials to create fuel in the crate. I expect you to bring me the most flammable you have ever made, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_104: There are heat-resistant lava rocks in the deposits east of Mol Iloh that can be used in the effigy's base. I expect you to bring me the finest one you can find, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_105: There is steppe sedge among the vegetation patches east of Mol Iloh that can be used for the papier-mache. I expect you to bring me a bundle of the finest you can find, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_106: There are invisible catfish in Nem Khaal, easily caught with salmon roe. We will need one for the ceremonial offering that will accompany the effigy burning. I expect you to bring me the finest one you can find, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_107: Gyorei will be the one collecting the components─all one hundred and seven of them. So speak to her when you are ready.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_108: And how it shall burn... Oh, you are still here? Right, right. Try the crate for more materials.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_100_108: And how it shall burn... Oh, you are still here? Right, right. Try the crate for more materials.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_110_108: And how it shall burn... Oh, you are still here? Right, right. Try the crate for more materials.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_200_108: And how it shall burn... Oh, you are still here? Right, right, Gyorei will collect your component.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_210_108: And how it shall burn... Oh, you are still here? Right, right, Gyorei will collect your component.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_220_108: And how it shall burn... Oh, you are still here? Right, right, Gyorei will collect your component.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_000_109: The crate appears to be filled to the brim with sundry materials─none of which you require at this time.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_100_109: The crate appears to be filled to the brim with sundry materials─none of which you require at this time.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_110_109: The crate appears to be filled to the brim with sundry materials─none of which you require at this time.

TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_000_110: You sift through the cornucopia of crafting materials and retrieve all you require for your work.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_100_110: You sift through the cornucopia of crafting materials and retrieve all you require for your work.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_110_110: You sift through the cornucopia of crafting materials and retrieve all you require for your work.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_111: You brought what I requested? That is a wise choice. An excellent decision!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOREI_000_112: I cannot say I expected us to go the “live sacrifice” route. No, no.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOREI_000_120: Gyoshin seems a bit odd. Though I suppose he is always odd...
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOREI_000_121: Ah, the final component! Thank you, thank you. Now let us see what comes of this.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_122: Wow, it is like looking into a stream. A reflection staring back at me! Most imposing. Quite impressive.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Gyoshin, are you not forgetting something? Yet again?
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_126: Oh! Thank you so much for volunteering!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: I most certainly am not volunteering! Should it not be the artist who sees his work through to the end?
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_128: Hm. Well, I am quite sure, indeed confident that  provided the most important parts...
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOREI_000_129: Oh, for the Big One's sake! You need not be in such a hurry to set each other aflame. According to Matoya's manuscript, a cloth doll is a perfectly acceptable substitute for the sacrifice. Yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOREI_000_130: I set my fins to sewing a few some time ago. And I followed the instructions to the letter, so they should be more than sufficient.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_GYOSHIN_000_132: Let us get this fire started!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_000_133: In seven years, the Namazu were fated to fall deeply in debt, and be doomed to work ceaselessly as slaves for the sinister soy sauce mogul, Kageyama. Many would have died.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_000_134: However, the oversized Namazu effigy will, over the course of seven years, come to be known far and wide as a uniquely bizarre spectacle, and generate significant revenue from tourism.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_000_135: Unbeknownst to all, the Namazu will be spared the grievous tragedy that could have consumed them, and their fate continues to change for the better.
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: I daresay it is impossible to discern the meaning or purpose behind this peculiar ritual. Indeed, it is nothing less than the epitome of enlightenment!
TEXT_BANNAM005_03101_SYSTEM_000_137: You have achieved Sworn reputation with the Namazu.

TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_001: Can you spare a moment? Just a bit of your time?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_002: You see, Gyorin has given us a gift of persimmons! But they are not just from him, no, no. They were paid for by many festival participants who wanted to give something to us, the organizers.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_003: According to Seigetsu the Enlightened, such gifts traditionally demonstrate gratitude for a fantastic festival! Or something like that. I dozed off, to be honest with you.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_004: Anyway, I think it would be quite fitting, most proper, to share this gift with everyone who made our festival a success. You will join me, yes, yes?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_005: Thank you! First we will pay a visit to Sadu in Dotharl Khaa. Off we go!
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOREI_000_015: I really must remain here to ensure that nothing catches on fire. Aside from the elements that are intended to be on fire, of course. But I will make arrangements to send thank-you gifts to the helpful shipwright and Matoya while you are away. Yes, yes. Please take my thanks to the Xaela!
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_020: Her gaze is still most cold, quite fearsome. Is her face stuck that way?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_SADU_000_030: You again. What is it this time?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_031: We are here to express our gratitude. To give thanks for your help with the archery contest! Via these persimmons from Namai, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_SADU_000_032: An odd gesture, but not unwelcome. I will taste this curious fruit.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_SADU_000_033: Word of your contest reached my ears. I would have dismissed it as mere rumor had my warriors not been the ones to deliver it. They said they nearly died of laughter.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_034: ...I am unsure whether that is a compliment or an insult. Yes, yes. But I am most pleased that you now know of the Namazu!
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_SADU_000_035: Ha! Nor will we soon forget. Stunted chuluu that you are.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_SADU_000_036: Our youths are eager to attend your festivities. You will entertain them.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_037: Of course, of course! Everyone is welcome! Just come to Dhoro Iloh sometime in the next seven years. We must set off for the Dawn Throne now, but I hope we meet again soon.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_040: Must he make that face? Is it necessary?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_SADU_000_041: I do want to eat this, but...how?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_MAGNAI_000_050: To our dismay, we have seen the enormous, grotesque statue you erected on the cliffs. It displeases us to suffer such an eyesore, though I will commend your artisans' skill.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_051: ...At least part of that was uncalled for. How uncivil. Anyway, we come bearing persimmons from Namai. As thanks for your explanation of Azim Bökh, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_MAGNAI_000_052: Ah, an offering. In that case, I will permit it.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_MAGNAI_000_053: The Oronir are always generous to those who pay obeisance. I will overlook your peculiar customs and grant the Namazu permission to hold your festival─at least until we claim victory in the next Naadam.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_MAGNAI_100_053: You may deliver the persimmons to Esugen. He has charge of all culinary matters.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_054: I am unsure whether we have an agreement or not, but I am quite satisfied that you at least know of the Namazu.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_MAGNAI_000_055: Indeed. Though at first I found your disfigured forms distasteful, I will allow that you too serve a purpose─not unlike the dzo─as do all the blessings of the Steppe.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_MAGNAI_000_056: One might be tempted to declare you superior to the Matanga, who lack your loquaciousness. Hm. Yes, I grant you leave to swear fealty to us as a tribe of the Steppe.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_057: ...Well, the rest of these persimmons are not getting any fresher! We must hurry to see the Mol. Make haste, yes, yes. See you around!
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_060: (Psst, ! She is still staring. Most raptly. Unceasingly. What do I do?)
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_MAGNAI_000_061: Lest you think I condone your behavior, know that I do not. For a khagan to cavort with Namazu bespeaks questionable judgment.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_CIRINA_000_070: <slurp> ...Oh! Pardon me. I didn't see you there, .
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_071: We have come bearing persimmons to thank you for your assistance! We could not have held our festival without the grounds you gave to us. No, no. And your insight into horse-racing was most appreciated.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_CIRINA_000_073: Dhoro Iloh seems so lively now─the festival must be going well. The children here do so wish to attend.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_074: They are most welcome! The Mol are free to attend any time, any time at all over the next seven years! We will be there.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_CIRINA_000_075: I look forward to it. And I'm sure the children will be delighted.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_CIRINA_000_076: I admit I thought it strange, that the udgan should speak of a person resembling a catfish. But I am happy to have met someone so delici─deft of hand.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_077: I am unsure whether you like me for my skill or for my flavor, yes, yes, but I thank you nonetheless! I hope to see you at Dhoro Iloh someday.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOREI_000_080: I have everything under control. Only intentional incineration here. Yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_CIRINA_000_081: These persimmons certainly are on the ripe side! I will make sure to serve them without delay.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_090: I would like to speak to everyone. Together! Please wait just one moment.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_091: Behold! Our majestic creation! So, um... Do you think it is impressive enough? Sufficiently inspiring of awe?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOREI_000_092: I find it curiously comforting. Yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: But of course! What could possibly express the spirit of enlightenment more effectively than an imposing sculpture?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_094: , do you think our festival has been...meaningful? Worthwhile? Will we be saved from our terrible fate?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_096: That is what I was worried about. What I feared.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_097: But I do not believe it matters. No, no. This festival brought us together. And together we made so many, many things.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_098: You really think so? Yes, yes?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_099: Even had it not, I would not regret it. No, no. This festival brought us together. And together we made so many, many things.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_100: Meaningful. Worthwhile. Valuable. Weighty words, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_101: But I think that what we do is what defines us. Crafting because we want to craft. Gathering because we want to gather. Even when no one sees its meaning, its worth, its value, we simply...do. That is what makes a disciple of creation.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Well said, Gyoshin! In fact, the same is recorded in A Meditation on the Metaphysics of Merrymaking. “In following our hearts we find a freedom, a peace, truer than any other─our own”!
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOREI_000_103: ...Gyofu─<sigh>─Seigetsu the Enlightened, is this really the time for citations?
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: I hope you do not imply I am being pretentious! Nothing could be further from the truth. I was bolstering Gyoshin's confidence by mentioning that I made the same observation in my debut publication: A Meditation on the Metaphysics of Merrymaking. I, too, am following my heart!
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_105: That is amazing, Seigetsu the Enlightened! I hope your heart leads you to summarize. To write succinctly.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_106: Oh! I nearly forgot for the fifth time. I have something for you.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_107: This is a deeply significant, most meaningful bell. I made it for you! With my own two fins. I am most grateful to everyone, but I am most most grateful to you, .
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_108: Our festival would not be the same without you. No, no.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_GYOSHIN_000_110: It seems we will be well occupied for the next seven years. Yes, yes!
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_SYSTEM_000_111: You have achieved Bloodsworn reputation with the Namazu.
TEXT_BANNAM006_03102_SYSTEM_000_112: You will receive an experience point bonus upon completion of the Namazu society daily quests.
TEXT_BANNAM301_03103_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Have you perchance encountered my errand boy? Grey, rotund fellow with a vacant gaze? No? I dispatched him with orders to procure additional happi materials some time ago, but have seen neither fin nor barbel of him since.

You surely recognize that I cannot waste my talents tracking wayward lackeys─the festival would collapse into uncivilized chaos were I to neglect my intellectual endeavors for but a moment. If you are not otherwise engaged, can you search for him in my stead?
His sojourn should have brought him to Mol Iloh, so you are likely to find him in the vicinity. If you discover him to have encountered complications, I trust you will ameliorate the situation.
TEXT_BANNAM301_03103_DAILYNAMAZUO03103_0: Woe, woe is me! I have encountered complications. If only someone would ameliorate them...
Oh! What a surprise to see you here, standing in silence mere ilms away. Yes, yes. Please never do it again.

I was absorbed in thought, you see. I had promised to trade with the Mol for materials we can use in our festive happi, and brought some fincrafted fineries along for this purpose. But then, when I least expected it...

...I was trampled by a charging dzo! It had dashed several malms by the time I regained my normal shape and the ability to walk. Yes, yes. I eventually discovered it devouring the last of my fineries.

...A flock of yol swooped down upon me! Luckily, I was able to liberate myself from their talons. Yes, yes. Less luckily, we were at least a malm in the air by then. By the time I regained solid ground and consciousness, my fineries were gone.
...I noticed several Buduga in pursuit! Hoping they would take my fineries instead of my life, I threw them behind me and ran. Yes, yes. Tossed them one and all.
I have no choice but to remake what I have lost. But I am only one Namazu, and require many fineries for trade. Will you lend me a fin?

TEXT_BANNAM301_03103_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: He is a hardworking fellow, but a veritable beacon for misfortune. I daresay his poor luck alone could bring about the Namazu's annihilation.
As for you, I have no doubt that your efforts this day will have a profound effect on the outcome of our festival, and contribute to the enlightenment of Namazu one and all. Probably.
TEXT_BANNAM302_03104_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Aha. Just the long-legged associate I was searching for. I have devised an addition to our event schedule. A pilgrimage! I trust you are available to participate?

As you are doubtless aware, the Namazu tribe originated on this very steppe, and traces of our heritage remain to this day. The pilgrimage will involve paying visit to those spiritual locations where our ancestors once trod. Well, swam. You take my meaning.

Our traditions include a particular orison: “In his whiskers' name.” Speak these words where the Hak Khaal cascades into the Sea of Blades, and at the shrine of Chakha Zoh. Of course, you are free to embellish on the prayer if you find it lacking in sophistication. I often do so myself.
TEXT_BANNAM302_03104_GUARD03104_005: Here we honor noble Chakha, so she may rest ever in glory. Never shall those who come to pay respects be turned away.
TEXT_BANNAM302_03104_WORSHIPNAMAZUO03104: This is apparently one of the Namazu's most holy, holiest of places. I will pray with gusto! In his whiskers' name, yes, yes.

In any case, the authenticity of the sites is irrelevant so long as pilgrims have a meaningful spiritual experience on which to build. Hingan traditions may be sophisticated now, but their ancients found spirituality through the worship of mountains, trees, and even fish. Fish!
TEXT_BANNAM303_03105_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Impeccable timing, . Under my exhaustive scrutiny, The Chrysanthemum and the Dango, page one hundred eighty-five, figure three, has revealed another important─I daresay indispensable─element of festival preparation. Purification of the venue!

If our event is to be a truly cultural affair, we mustn't neglect this preliminary ritual. Thus, I took the liberty of hiring a man to prepare the necessary implements─but I worry he fails to grasp their significance. Pray seek him at Tao Khaal and impress upon him the gravity of his task.

Indeed, our festival must aim for ever greater heights of incomprehensibility if we are to reach true enlightenment. Our course forward is clear!
TEXT_BANNAM304_03106_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Doth the sun, in her midday glory, outshine the moon of a night silent and solitary? No, of course I am not interested in your opinion. I was simply waxing poetic.

The inspiration for my lyrical musings, if you must know, is our latest festival conundrum. We have decided to keep the festival running through the night, and Gyoshin now clamors ceaselessly for more brazier components.

I have assigned the task of acquiring said components to one of our volunteers already, but perhaps you had best assist him. Why he insisted on bearing a massive crate of materials out to Ceol Aen is beyond me, but it should make finding him a simple matter.

TEXT_BANNAM305_03107_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: I say, , attempting to organize seven hundred seventy-seven Namazu for this festival is like herding catfish! Having─to my misfortune─grown up amongst these simpletons, I suspect we might elicit more enthusiasm were we to offer souvenirs. My brethren love nothing more than complimentary trinkets, no matter how useless. Thus, I designed uchiwa fans that we can distribute to encourage participation.

Alas, though I began instructing a fellow in their assembly, he trundled off midway through my explanation─with my crate of supplies, no less! It looked as if he was headed for the northern edge of Azim Khaat. You must locate him and ensure that he remembers to provide me the components I asked for.

TEXT_BANNAM305_03107_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: I presume that you, at least, managed to focus on the task at hand?
Excellent work. I am confident that providing colorful uchiwa free of charge will attract Namazu to our festival in droves. As much as I disdain their simplemindedness, it does have its uses.
TEXT_BANNAM305_03107_KOFUINSEIGETSU_100_: Excellent work─I will have these materials processed posthaste. I am confident that providing colorful uchiwa free of charge will attract Namazu to our festival in droves. As much as I disdain their simplemindedness, it does have its uses.
TEXT_BANNAM305_03107_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: And, I might add, these shows of benevolence are vital if I am to lead the Namazu from the mire of ignorance in which they languish. As The Princeling so astutely advises, a leader should be both feared and loved by the masses!
TEXT_BANNAM306_03108_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: , do you comprehend the true essence of “civilization”? Indeed, culture is a vital element─but so is society. There can be no civilization without advanced relationships between individuals and, I assert, peoples.

Yes, what makes a group civilized is its productive interactions with others. Moreover, history shows that those who eschew relationships with neighboring societies do so not just to their detriment, but at their peril.

That is why I have taken the initiative in preparing gifts for our neighbors, the Uyagir. Their goodwill is essential not only to the success of our festival, but to the enlightenment of Namazu one and all!

I sent the most affable fellow I could find to make the delivery. I am certain that of the six dozen or so Namazu I interviewed, he would be the last to cause offense. And yet, I cannot shake the feeling that something has gone awry─I cannot rest until you, personally, make for Ceol Aen to find him!

TEXT_BANNAM306_03108_BAAVGAI_000_053: I apologize if our strict ways make us seem ungrateful. The unbridled greed of our forefathers led our tribe to ruin, so we must be vigilant not to repeat their mistakes.

TEXT_BANNAM306_03108_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Ah, so he was detained designing gifts more to Uyagiri tastes. Narrow Road through the Deep Grass mentioned their preference for simplicity, but I did not anticipate how stringent their requirements would be.
As always, I appreciate your assistance in strengthening our ties with the Xaela. It is undoubtedly the enlightened thing to do!
TEXT_BANNAM401_03109_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: As we prepare for the festival, the committee members strive to outdo each other by procuring ever more unusual offerings. Some have started looking to local folktales for inspiration.
One such story speaks of an enormous catfish which lurks in Azim Khaat. A self-proclaimed “master fisher” has left in search of the beast.
However, this was some time ago, and he should have either caught it or conceded defeat by now. I would have him return posthaste, preferably with something to show for his expedition.
Assist him with any means at your disposal. Or failing that, a swift kick in the direction of Dhoro Iloh will suffice.
TEXT_BANNAM401_03109_DAILYNAMAZUO03109_0: Seigetsu is growing impatient is he? But I can't go back now! I've finally found the “Great Barbeled One!” The trouble is, she's taken a liking to my lures and has eaten them all.
TEXT_BANNAM401_03109_DAILYNAMAZUO03109_1: So Seigetsu sent you to help me land this freshwater leviathan, the “Great Barbeled One,” did he?
TEXT_BANNAM401_03109_DAILYNAMAZUO03109_0: Perhaps you could wiggle those digits of yours and make me parts for some more catfish lures? You'll find the raw materials and whatnot in that crate.
Perhaps you could wiggle those digits of yours and make me parts for some more catfish lures? You'll find the raw materials and whatnot in that crate.
Perhaps you could make the scented, smelly things we attach to catfish lures? You'll find the raw materials and whatnot in that crate.

To make matters worse, I've run out of the shiny steppe geodes needed to make more lures! Wait─ Is that a pickaxe you've got there? Maybe you'd like to help a master fisher pursue his prey by mining the necessary twinkly things, yes, yes?

To make matters worse, I've run out of the pretty yol feathers needed to make more lures! You smell like you're used to scrabbling around in the dirt, yes, yes? And good at finding things among the plants, I'll wager! Maybe your green fingers can gather some feathers for me!

Think you can catch her all by yourself, do you? I don't suppose you'll fare any better than me, but I'd like to see you try, yes, yes! And since I'm feeling generous, I'll give you some advice: She seems to enjoy salmon roe...
Bring them to me when you've finished!
TEXT_BANNAM401_03109_DAILYNAMAZUO03109_1: On the off chance you manage to land the “Great Barbeled One” before I do, bring her to me for inspection. I'll know if you try to deceive me!
TEXT_BANNAM401_03109_DAILYNAMAZUO03109_0: I brought a crate full of metallic, shiny bits for lures, forgetting that I can't make them myself. Very silly of me, yes, yes.
I brought a crate full of bits and pieces for making lures, forgetting that I can't do it myself. Very silly of me, yes, yes.
Ingredients for the smelly things I have, yes, yes. Knowledge and dexterity needed to make use of them, I have not. Quite the oversight, I'm sure you will agree.

TEXT_BANNAM401_03109_DAILYNAMAZUO03109_0: Having trouble finding the shinies? There should be some to the northeast of Azim Khaat. Yes, yes.
Having trouble finding the feathers? There should be some to the northeast of Azim Khaat. Yes, yes.
Be careful not to fall into the lake. The “Great Barbeled One” will lose her appetite if she eats you, and I can't have that. No, no.
So, do you have something to show me?
How goes your fishing? Caught something noteworthy, have you?
Splendid! My success is all but a foregone conclusion now, yes, yes. You can run along to Seigetsu and tell him I'll be back with an offering so auspicious, he'll regret ever doubting me!
Such a vast and impressive fish! I must admit, you've outdone me on this occasion.

But it's not over yet! As big as your catch is, I believe she is still a juvenile, judging by the growth rings on the fins. That means that larger adults must be nearby, yes, yes. The real “Great Barbeled One” yet lurks in these waters!
I'll keep your fish here so that I can measure it against my own catches. Tell Seigetsu that I will only return when I have triumphed over a catfish fit for the festival!
My true prize yet evades me. You go on ahead and tell Seigetsu to stop fretting!
TEXT_BANNAM401_03109_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: He is still out there!? Instead of bringing him back, you have provided him with the means to waste even more time. And as for this so-called “Great Barbeled One,” I will believe it when I see it!
This is not the outcome I was hoping for. He now pursues a fish even larger and more elusive than his original target!

If this catfish is as gargantuan as he claims, he is likely to find himself dragged into the lake and swallowed whole. Not that it is any concern of mine, of course, but having one less pair of fins to deal with menial tasks would interfere with my plans to some degree.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: It appears a miscalculation has been made. But not by me─ Perish the thought!

The amount of timber we require for the festival far exceeds that which can be harvested within a reasonable distance of Dhoro Iloh. As you can see, although the Azim Steppe has an abundance of grass, trees are few and far between.

As luck would have it, Gyorin has arrived in Reunion, bearing timber to barter for local goods. I took the liberty of arranging for you to meet him. However, I will leave the particulars of the trade to you.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_011: I never imagined that you would be the one sent by Seigetsu the Egregious, or whatever he calls himself. Without further ado, let's get down to business, shall we? Yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_012: Back again, ? Need some more wood, do you?
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_013: I'm not sure why you're still running errands for Seigetsu the Intolerable. Having said that, I am always thrilled to do business with one as well-mannered as yourself!
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_014: I come in search of goods that my clients at The New Rich would find intriguing, and more importantly, be willing to purchase.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_015: I notice that many inhabitants of the Azim Steppe wear exquisitely crafted necklaces that I believe would fetch a high price. I'd like you to craft enough pieces to make one. I can take care of the rest, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_016: During my travels through the Azim Steppe, I have seen a variety of distinctive zukin, or “headdresses,” as you might call them. I'd like you to craft enough pieces to make one. I can take care of the rest, yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_017: Some of the locals partake in the imbibing of kumis. I have obtained a quantity of mare's milk, but I gather the fermentation process is rather complicated and involves a lot of stirring. Perhaps you can prepare the basic ingredients, yes, yes?
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_018: The rocky outcrops in the southern parts of the Azim Steppe contain gems unlike those seen anywhere else, known as raw azimite. Bring a finful of these rarities to me and the timber is yours!
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_019: The southern parts of the Azim Steppe are home to a valuable species of steppe candyfruit. Bring a few of these to me and the timber is yours!
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_020: The Nem Khaal is teeming with rainbow killifish, native to this region. I'd like a sample to show my customers. Just one will suffice, yes, yes! I heard they like salmon roe, so try using that as bait.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_021: I'll watch over the merchandise until you return.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_022: You need more materials? Help yourself─ There are plenty more.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_023: You need more materials? Help yourself─ There are plenty more.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_024: Was there a problem with the fermentation? Not stirring vigorously enough, perhaps? I have more ingredients, so use as much as you need.

TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_034: Have any of those rainbow killifish found their way onto your hook yet?
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_040: Have you brought the goods I seek?
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_041: Perfect! Now production of authentic local goods can begin!
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_042: Customers from far and wide will flock to The New Rich for such fine wares. Yes, yes!
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_043: If I can ensure a steady flow of stock from the Azim Steppe, my profits will go through the roof!
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_044: You've kept your part of the bargain, so I will do likewise. This finest-quality Yanxian timber now belongs to the Seven Hundred Seventy-Seven.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_045: Be sure to tell Seigetsu the Insufferable that I am willing to supply further shipments, although I would prefer to avoid dealing directly with that pompous nincompoop.
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_GYORIN_000_046: Can I rely on you to act as our intermediary, our go-between?
TEXT_BANNAM402_03110_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Would I be correct in assuming that our business with Gyorin has come to a satisfactory conclusion?
Ah, superlative work, ! While Gyorin may be an unsophisticated boor, his mercantile acumen is commendable, and he no doubt has access to other wares that would benefit our cause.
As for the timber, I will put it to good use. And by that, I mean order my underlings to put it to good use.
TEXT_BANNAM403_03111_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: The Chrysanthemum and the Dango describes a Hingan ritual in which the spirits of their ancestors are beckoned into the home to ensure a bountiful harvest.
We will perform these selfsame rites here in Dhoro Iloh. Should the souls of our forebears answer the call, their divine protection may prove instrumental in averting our impending doom.

One of the Seven Hundred Seventy-Seven is searching the plains for the necessary offerings. As this was not originally a custom of the Namazu, there may be matters best handled by someone with...hands. Think of it as another opportunity to prove your usefulness!
TEXT_BANNAM403_03111_DAILYNAMAZUO03111_0: Did Gyofun...I mean, Seigetsu the Enlightened send you? I'm so inundated with tasks, I can't possibly manage them alone. I need your help!
We need traditional serving trays to present the food for the kami! Please, look inside that crate and see if there's anything you can use!
We need a traditional serving mat to present the offerings! Please, look inside that crate and see if there's anything you can use!
We need traditional delicacies to present as offerings! Please, look inside that crate and see if there's anything you can use!
I was told to gather steppe clay for making traditional Hingan crockery. You'll go and get some for me, won't you? Try searching a little south of Chakha Zoh. Yes, yes.

I was told to gather ingredients for traditional Hingan dishes, but I can't find any edible buds! I heard they grow south of Chakha Zoh, but I couldn't find any for the life of me. Perhaps you will have better luck. Yes, yes.
We need a steppe sweetfish, the centerpiece of the offerings! Could you catch one from Tao Khaal? Apparently, they are drawn to the smell of salmon roe. Yes, yes.
When you're done, please go straight to Seigetsu. He is insistent that he is the only one capable of arranging the offerings as tradition dictates. Yes, yes.
Did you have a mishap? Not to worry, there are more materials in the crate.
Did you have a mishap? Not to worry, there are more materials in the crate.
So the delicacy didn't turn out as well as you'd hoped? Not to worry, there are more ingredients in the crate.

TEXT_BANNAM403_03111_DAILYNAMAZUO03111_0: You can't find any steppe clay? Try looking south of Chakha Zoh.
You can't find any edible buds? Try looking south of Chakha Zoh.
Are the steppe sweetfish eluding you? There should be plenty in Tao Khaal. Yes, yes.
You've done ever so well! I'm sure Seigetsu will approve. Yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM403_03111_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Do you have something to present to me?
Let me see... Yes, yes, perfectly adequate. Once the offerings have been suitably blessed and arranged, all that will remain is to perform the ritual itself.
Part of the ceremony involves enacting a banquet as though our long-dead ancestors are corporeally present. The process is extremely lengthy and involves chanting in an ancient Hingan tongue.
I dare not entrust such a delicate task to any of my Namazu brethren, who would no doubt botch the incantations and leave us all cursed to eternal damnation.
TEXT_BANNAM404_03112_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: One particular custom I wish to include in our festival involves the parading of several mikoshi. But this is not like before, no, no. Each will be carried by a group of Namazu and made to crash into the other mikoshi, as tradition dictates.
In contrast to the boisterous and potentially dangerous nature of this practice, the mikoshi themselves are intricately carved and lavishly decorated. However, we lack the proper tools.

I believe we can avoid wasting coin on such instruments by fabricating our own from a dzo horn. One should provide enough raw material for several chisels. All I ask is your assistance in obtaining said horn from a local dzoherd.
I have arranged a meeting between yourself and one such individual at the Dawn Throne. Perhaps you can offer your services in exchange for the goods we seek?
TEXT_BANNAM404_03112_DAILYORONIR03112_00: Are you here for the dzo horn? No need to explain─ The little squeaking fellow told me all about it.
I have been a dzoherd for twenty years─as a boy and then a man. Yet never have I heard tell of their horns being fashioned into tools.
When a dzo is slaughtered, nothing goes to waste. Every part has value, so I cannot simply give you what you seek. I propose a trade.
Dzos are covered in thick, coarse hair which cannot be allowed to grow too long. The shears wear down quickly and must be replaced. Take what you need from this box and craft new blades.

Dzos are covered in thick, coarse hair which cannot be allowed to grow too long. Shear handles break with much use, and we are in need of more. Take what you need from this box and craft replacements.

Dzos are covered in thick, coarse hair which cannot be allowed to grow too long. We use honing oil to keep our shears sharp. If you can prepare some more oil with the ingredients in this box, the horn is yours.

Dzos are covered in thick, coarse hair which cannot be allowed to grow too long. We use steppe whetstones to keep our shears sharp. Bring me two and we have a deal. They can be found to the northeast of the Dawn Throne.
You have come at a good time. We are in need of grazing grass used in dzo feed. Bring me some and we have a deal. You will find it to the northeast of the Dawn Throne.

You have come at a good time. We are in need of fish oil used in dzo feed. Although dzos only eat plants and grasses, the oil aids their digestion. Go to Azim Khaat and catch a greasy strangler. Our fishers normally use salmon roe as bait.
When you are ready to trade, come to me.
If you need more materials, help yourself.
If you need more materials, help yourself.
If you need more ingredients, help yourself.

TEXT_BANNAM404_03112_DAILYORONIR03112_00: Did you try looking to the northeast of the Dawn Throne?
Did you try looking to the northeast of the Dawn Throne?
If you are thinking about jumping down to Azim Khaat, look before you leap. The rocks below have claimed the lives of many a young fool.
Do you have what I need?
Exactly what I was looking for! Your efforts are much appreciated.
And now for me to fulfill my part of the bargain.
I suppose you will be returning to Dhoro Iloh now? Please tell your friends that I would welcome similar exchanges in the future.
I hope that the dzo horn tools serve their purpose. This could be the beginning of a new trade for me.
TEXT_BANNAM404_03112_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: If you've brought the horn, I will inspect it immediately.

Yes, this appears to be of an acceptable standard. Once again, I have demonstrated remarkable foresight in selecting you for this task. Now I must choose which of my minions will be transforming this horn into tools for carving the mikoshi.
You may ask why we are putting so much effort into creating such ornate mikoshi if they are destined to be smashed to pieces. They are merely a means to end.
Through their construction we further our abilities as artisans. The hoisting, chanting, and violent collisions display the vim and vigor of the Namazu.
TEXT_BANNAM404_03112_SYSTEM_000_054: Normal-quality items crafted in the course of this quest serve no purpose and cannot be sold. It is recommended that you discard them.
TEXT_BANNAM405_03113_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Sluggards! Layabouts! Good-for-nothing reprobates! The festival preparations will never be complete at this rate! When will they learn? They will be allowed rest, water, and nourishment when, and only when, their duties are complete! I require a solution to this quandary.
The key, I believe, lies in Narrow Road through the Deep Grass. It describes a traditional dish of the Azim Steppe known as “buuz,” a steamed bun with remarkable recuperative properties.

Giving the workers buuz should temporarily revitalize them and ensure that the work is finished in time for the festival. The buuz will be made here in Dhoro Iloh, in exact accordance with the recipe outlined in my tome.

I have tasked one of the Seven Hundred Seventy-Seven with gathering the necessary ingredients and apparatus. I want you to verify that he is acting precisely as instructed and not filling his face with marketplace fare.
TEXT_BANNAM405_03113_DAILYNAMAZUO03113_0: <munch> Seigetsu sent you? <munch> No, no, I'm not sampling the delectable local cuisine, not at all. <munch> You're here to help with the buuz, yes, yes?

I want to serve them freshly steamed, but for that I'll need a certain type of pot. Could you try making a couple from the metal things that I gathered? I was planning to buy some, but the money Seigetsu gave me mysteriously vanished. Yes, yes. <belch>

I want to serve them freshly cooked, but for that I'll need some special bamboo steamers. Could you try making a couple from the materials that I gathered? I was planning to buy some, but the money Seigetsu gave me mysteriously vanished. Yes, yes. <belch>
Seigetsu specified that the dough should be made exactly as written in that book of his. You can do that for me, yes, yes? The necessary ingredients are in that crate.
Seigetsu wants to build a hearth for steaming the buuz and specified that we use steppe soapstones. Apparently, they can be found south of Reunion.

I've been told that we need something called a “steppe onion” but I'm clueless when it comes to plants. I've been told they grow south of Reunion, but I wouldn't know one if it jumped up and bit me on the barbel!

Seigetsu's recipe uses grass shrimp that live in the Nem Khaal. But I'm much too exhausted for fishing. I can barely keep my eyes open as it is. Perhaps you could catch one for me? According to the locals, salmon roe is the best bait to use.
Please, you go on ahead. I'll be resting my tired fins here. I think I need a little nap after all that food I've been─I mean, all that hard work I've been doing!
Do you need more materials? Please, take whatever you need. There'll be less for me to carry back that way. Yes, yes.
Do you need more materials? Please, take whatever you need. There'll be less for me to carry back that way. Yes, yes.
Do you need more ingredients? Please, take whatever you need. There'll be less for me to carry back that way. Yes, yes.

TEXT_BANNAM405_03113_DAILYNAMAZUO03113_0: Struggling to find steppe soapstones? They should be nearby. Yes, yes.
Struggling to find steppe onions? They should be nearby. Yes, yes.
Have you been to Nem Khaal? I heard the grass shrimp are abundant.
<yawn> Oh, back so soon?
Thank you! You've saved me a lot of hard work, yes, yes!
Do you know, this isn't the first time we've eaten buuz. We once bought some in Reunion that were heavenly! If the buuz we make are even half as good, we are all in for a treat. Yes, yes!
We actually tried to cook buuz before with buzzfly meat, but it was a catastrophe! Many of us were so sick we couldn't move for days. Hopefully this time there will be fewer casualties. Yes, yes.
I tried making a small batch of buuz before but the reception was...shall we say, lukewarm at best. I'm good at eating buuz, not so good at cooking them, it seems.
I think I'll ask some of the locals for advice before I start cooking. If I make a mess of things, I'll never hear the end of it! Could you tell Seigetsu I'll be back soon?
It's unusual for Seigetsu to go to such lengths─rather, order someone else to go to such lengths─for the sake of us workers. Methinks he has ulterior motives. Yes, yes...
TEXT_BANNAM405_03113_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Well? Did you find him? What did he have to say for himself?
He seeks the counsel of local culinarians? Entirely unnecessary. He will prepare the buuz exactly as is detailed in Narrow Road through the Deep Grass, to the letter.

Trivialities such as “flavor” are of no concern. The sole objective is to keep the workers ali─I mean, motivated─long enough for my grand scheme to come to fruition. For your part in said scheme, you have my thanks.
TEXT_BANNAM406_03114_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Many civilized peoples of Othard perform rituals in which wine is offered to the kami. To prove that we are equally sophisticated, I propose that we host a similar ceremony.

However, rather than wine, we Namazu become inebriated by drinking tea. Since the offering of an intoxicating beverage appears to be the focal point of the proceedings, we will substitute the wine with tea.
Coincidentally, the Mol tribe perform a ceremony in which tea is presented to the old gods. I have sent an envoy to learn of their customs so that we may perform our own version here in Dhoro Iloh.
Unfortunately, he has been gone longer than I had anticipated. Perhaps the Mol are slowly roasting him over a fire! Ha! But joking aside, he may be dead. Please investigate his whereabouts.
TEXT_BANNAM406_03114_DAILYNAMAZUO03114_0: Seigetsu asked you to look for me? I always thought he was utterly heartless, but perhaps he is not so bad after all.

Well, having said that, he has set me a rather difficult task. Not only was I told to participate in a Mol tea ceremony, he also ordered me to gather all the things necessary to recreate the ritual, right down to the most minute detail!
TEXT_BANNAM406_03114_DAILYNAMAZUO03114_1: The number of different knickknacks needed to make a simple cup of “buurtsag tsai” is mind-boggling! And then there are all the complicated steps involved in the ceremony itself. Please, you've got to help me!
TEXT_BANNAM406_03114_DAILYNAMAZUO03114_0: The Mol use a special teapot to brew the tea. Very large and heavy it is. If you could craft one using the materials I've collected, I'd be extremely grateful.
The Mol use a tea strainer when pouring the tea. Very different to the ones we Namazu use, yes, yes. If you could craft one using the materials I've collected, I'd be extremely grateful.
The Mol sweeten their tea with a mixture of sugar and spices. If you could make some using the ingredients I've collected, I'd be extremely grateful.
Naturally, only a certain type of water is used in the ritual, steppe spring water, in fact. Do you think you could get some for me? The Mol say it springs forth east of Mol Iloh.
I was surprised to see them add fava beans to the pot while brewing the tea! Apparently they grow east of Mol Iloh, but I couldn't find any. Could you collect some for me?

I was surprised to see them pour the tea using a flagon clam! It seemed a little awkward to me, but we must stay true to the Mol traditions, yes, yes. Could you go to Hak Khaal and fetch one for me? The best bait to use is salmon roe, according to local fishers.
Once you've taken care of that, I think I'll be ready for the ceremony. Let me know when you're done.
Oh, not enough materials? There should be some more in the box.
Oh, not enough materials? There should be some more in the box.

TEXT_BANNAM406_03114_DAILYNAMAZUO03114_0: I heard the best place to collect steppe spring water is east of Mol Iloh, yes, yes. Have you tried looking around there?
I heard the best place to gather fava beans is east of Mol Iloh, yes, yes. Have you tried looking around there?
The Mol go to Hak Khaal for their flagon clam. Might be a good place to start, yes, yes?
Have you brought the last of the tea ceremony things?
Tremendous! Exactly the same as the Mol use! I've boiled some water to make a simplified version of the tea for Seigetsu to try. One moment, please.
Here you are. It might taste a little different once we start using the authentic teapot, but this should be close enough. Yes, yes.
I'm going to practice brewing the tea before going back to perform the ritual. I have to make sure the flavor is just right.
TEXT_BANNAM406_03114_DAILYNAMAZUO03114_1: Don't worry, I won't drink myself into a stupor, I promise! Tell Seigetsu that although I left as a novice, I will return as a master of...pouring tea! Yes, yes.
TEXT_BANNAM406_03114_DAILYNAMAZUO03114_0: No, no, I'll be fine here. If I am attacked by a wild beast, my shrieks of terror are sure to alert the Mol villagers, who will rush to my aid. Probably.
TEXT_BANNAM406_03114_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: So, did you find him in one piece? And more importantly, what about the tea?
Not only did he witness their customs, but he has already made tea in the traditional Mol fashion? Interesting. However, I shall withhold my praise until I have sampled the fruits of his labor.
<slurp> Hmmm... A complex infusion of leguminous and earthy notes that stimulates the palate, with a residually floral finish. Certainly a gift fit for the kami or the old gods.

Upon his return, I will have him pour cup after cup. Naturally, once the kami have been given their share, the remainder will be distributed amongst those most deserving. By that, I am mainly referring to myself, but the others are welcome to my dregs.

Is that disdain I detect in your expression? Spare me. Decadent rulers and underprivileged lower classes are the hallmarks of a civilized society, and we Namazu are no different. I have my role, and the plebeians have theirs.
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: It is an unfortunate fact that whilst the collision of cultures is often an enriching affair for all concerned, a sudden encounter with the unfamiliar can just as easily lead to conflict. As such, we cannot assume that the Xaela will accept us with open arms.

No, should matters come to blows, those proud warrior people could have every one of us steamed and served in a buuz─in the most disturbingly literal fashion─which would put quite a damper on efforts to refine our civilization.

Thus did I bend my intellect to the task of how we might avoid such an unpleasant fate. After much deliberation, I was rewarded with the most ingenious idea: we shall exhibit our peaceful intentions to the Xaela by paying our respects to their gods!
Go now, ! Gyotaku will provide you with a mikoshi, that you might float with serene purpose to the sacred sites of the Azim Steppe.

A number of my kin have already begun their pilgrimage, and await your arrival at the Dusk Throne. When the Xaela witness you leading the devotions of our people from atop the mikoshi, they will surely recognize the harmonious significance of your presence!
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_GYOTAKU_000_010: You have come for a mikoshi, yes, yes? Hop on board, and honor those Xaela gods with a rousing Namazu wasshoi!
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_GYOTAKU_100_010: When the others returned with the mikoshi, I had thought your mission successfully completed. But it seems you simply hopped down...or tumbled off. Here, why don't you try again, and keep a tighter grip this time, yes, yes?
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_DAILYNAMAZUO03115_0: Dusky goddess, we come to offer our respects! We hope our display of worship meets with your approval!
I wonder if the goddess minds being buried in the sand like that... A Namazu would just dry right out! Shrivel right up! We'll have to continue our visits and keep Her company!

The goddess is so expansive, the way Her magnificence fills your vision... I felt an itch in my fins to just start climbing and nestle myself i─ Hm? Of course I didn't clamber up this sacred statue! No, no!
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_DAILYNAMAZUO03115_1: Our duty is done. Your wasshoi was wonderful, ! Most devotional! Now we must present ourselves at the Dawn Throne. See you there, yes? Yes, yes!
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_DAILYNAMAZUO03115_0: Do not be alarmed─we are the Namazu from atop the Towering Still! We have put aside our festival preparations to come before the gods of the Azim Steppe and pay the proper obeisance!
As our friend here has demonstrated from atop the mikoshi, a spirited wasshoi is the Namazu way of showing respect!
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_ORONIRMAN03115A_000: I might think you come to insult us...but if the champion of the Naadam acts on your behalf, then we must accept the sincerity of your words.
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_ORONIRMAN03115B_000: Thank you for accompanying these...envoys. I saw only finned creatures flapping towards us, and thought catfish had dragged themselves up from the Azim Khaat. I was close to kicking them into the water...
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_DAILYNAMAZUO03115_0: Seigetsu the Enlightened has ordered─very firmly suggested─that we perform our greetings on a regular basis. And so here we are!
Gods and mortals, natives and visitors alike, may we all be filled with festive spirit!
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_ORONIRMAN03115A_000: Again, you come. Again we struggle to understand your ways. And again we will recognize your efforts to show respect, as odd as they are...
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_ORONIRMAN03115B_000: These unique displays of worship have captured the attention of many of our people. The Namazu are fortunate you chose to participate─they might otherwise have been seen as a threat, rather than a confusing curiosity.
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_DAILYNAMAZUO03115_1: And now we must return to our tasks. Peace be with you! And with you, !
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_ORONIRMAN03115B_110: We, too, must return to our duties. Know that you are welcome to approach again should you wish to entertai─ahem, “honor” us with another show of respect.
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_DAILYNAMAZUO03115_0: We are but humble Namazu! Bear witness as we demonstrate our respect for your mighty deities!
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_SYSTEM_000_025: The Namazu have approached the Oronir. Speak with Gyotaku at Dhoro Iloh to mount a mikoshi, and perform a rousing Wasshoi before the Dawn Throne.
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_DAILYNAMAZUO03115_1: We're ready for the wasshoi now. Let's make it a good one!
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_SYSTEM_000_026: The Namazu are waiting to perform their greeting alongside the mikoshi. Speak with Gyotaku at Dhoro Iloh to mount a mikoshi, and perform a rousing Wasshoi before the Dusk Throne.
TEXT_BANNAM501_03115_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: I thank you for leading our people in the pursuit of harmony. Tell me, were the Xaela receptive to our overtures?

Ah, just as I suspected: your presence is essential for fostering an atmosphere of acceptance, if not outright trust. The mutual understanding gained through the exchange of cultures is truly a marvelous thing, and it is a road that we must continue to pave if we would improve our civilization.
TEXT_BANNAM502_03116_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: , do you recall the horse racing tradition shared with us by the Mol? Well, we should like to continue with our own ceremonial races, but by my educated estimations, we are lacking certain supplies vital for the care of our horses.
Whilst my own knowledge in such areas is purely theoretical, I imagine that you, as a productive member of the civilized races, would find the practice of raising livestock a trivial affair, yes?

A fortunate thing indeed, for although I entrusted the gathering of said supplies to our appointed horse handler, I fear he has failed to return. I suspect he has encountered difficulties. Please look for him in the vicinity of Ceol Aen, and uncover the cause of this delay.
TEXT_BANNAM502_03116_DAILYNAMAZUO03116_0: <sigh> I'm putting together as many of the stable supplies as I'm able, but I've not enough fins to handle all these tasks.
Would you mind making some horseshoes for me? The crate just there should hold everything you need.
Would you mind making some grooming brushes for me? The crate just there should hold everything you need.
Would you mind making some bridle oil for me? The crate just there should hold everything you need.
Would you mind digging up some steppe iron for me? We need it for making horseshoes. The rocks to the south of Chakha Zoh should have a vein or two you can mine.
Would you mind gathering some fodder for the horses? The foliage to the south of Chakha Zoh should do nicely. It's so dry, they call it “steppe hay,” apparently.

Would you mind finding some salmon roe for bait, and fishing up a moon oyster from Tao Khaal? It can be made into an ointment for soothing saddle sores and the like. Or so Seigetsu told me. At great length.
Once you've prepared these absolutely essential supplies, please deliver them directly to Seigetsu. I'll see that my share of the goods is not far behind!
What's the matter? Have you misplaced your materials? There should be plenty more in my little crate. It's deceptively roomy!

There should be moon oysters in the waters of Tao Khaal. I hear with a little salmon roe, they jump right onto your hook!
You have the supplies I asked of you? Then please make your delivery directly to Seigetsu before he comes to “enlighten” us on the merits of haste!
TEXT_BANNAM502_03116_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Ah, so you located our aspiring horse handler. ...Not flattened under a khun chuluu, was he?

Not enough fins to finish his tasks!? Well he cannot rely on you to pick up the slack every time a job proves too overwhelming. We shall have to discuss the allocation of his duties upon his return. At length.

If things progress in this manner, I wonder if we shall ever prove suitable masters for our stables. With our stunted limbs, Namazu struggle to cling to a horse's back as it is, and we certainly cannot direct the beasts to gallop where we wish.

On that front, I have been perusing the anatomical journals of past and present, researching a method for the permanent elongation of fins and legs. My current goal is to evolve our species to stand some eight heads tall.

On the dawn that such an evolution is realized, the name of Seigetsu the Enlightened will be burned forever into the pages of Namazu history. I shall be lauded as a hero of our civilization, and you, my friend, might even gain a mention in the footnotes!
TEXT_BANNAM503_03117_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: According to that most puissant publication, The Chrysanthemum and the Dango, music has always been an indispensable part of festivals. And if our celebration is to beat with the requisite celebratory rhythm, then we must perforce acquire ourselves the necessary instruments.

Simply purchasing instruments would, however, cheapen the spirit of the event. In my literature-enriched opinion, the sound of drums crafted from locally sourced materials will best resonate with the souls of our steppe-dwelling ancestors.

I have volunteered Gyoshin to assemble our music-making paraphernalia, but we await integral parts and pieces from one of our apprentice artisans. Would you please find him over near Chakha Zoh, and expedite the crafting process?
TEXT_BANNAM503_03117_DAILYNAMAZUO03117_0: Ah, you're a clever one with your fins, yes, yes? I've been putting together bits and pieces for our festival instruments, and just realized I was missing a piece here and a bit there.
Could you do me a favor, and hammer out a batch of pins for securing drum skins? My crate here should have everything you need.
Could you do me a favor, and shape some leather into drum skins? My crate here should have everything you need.
Could you do me a favor, and mix up some lacquer for coating drum shells? My crate here should have everything you need.
Could you do me a favor, and pick me out a pair of nice flat stones for tanning drum skins? Two would be plenty! More than enough. I think I saw some likely candidates to the south of here...
Could you do me a favor, and pick me a basket or two of tea leaves for tanning drum skins? Yes, yes, two would be plenty! More than enough. I think I saw some tea plants to the south of here...

Could you do me a favor, and get your fins on a leatherscale? Seigetsu is convinced that if we stretch out the fish's skin and clamp it down, it should make a satisfying percussive boom! Try your rod in the waters of the upper Yat Khaal─a little salmon roe on the hook should do the trick.
Ah, once you've taken care of my little favor, you can deliver it straight to Seigetsu. Many, many thanks in advance!
Have you fumbled my favor? If you want to try again, there's more than enough materials in my crate! ...Please, please try again.

TEXT_BANNAM503_03117_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Are we to see a complete delivery of drum parts today? Or was our neophyte artisan too busy splashing his fins in the stream?
TEXT_BANNAM503_03117_KOFUINSEIGETSU_100_: Ah, this is exactly the sort of crafting expertise I anticipated. It would seem I was justified in enlisting your assistance.
TEXT_BANNAM503_03117_KOFUINSEIGETSU_110_: Ah, this is exactly the sort of geological expertise I anticipated. It would seem I was justified in enlisting your assistance.

TEXT_BANNAM503_03117_KOFUINSEIGETSU_130_: Ah, this is exactly the sort of piscatological expertise I anticipated. It would seem I was justified in enlisting your assistance.
TEXT_BANNAM503_03117_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: The lively beat of our grand festival will echo ever more loudly across the steppe now that our number of drums is set to multiply.
Our celebrations have begun to reverberate with such ear-shattering volume, in fact, that I can scarce concentrate on my reading...
But such is the price of progress─whensoever we shed light upon the walls of civilization, we cannot help but create pools of shadow...
TEXT_BANNAM504_03118_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: A fellow festival enthusiast volunteered to return one of the horses the Mol so graciously provided for our racing event, but I fear his “enthusiasm” is rather greater than his horsemanship...
To be perfectly blunt, he is an atrocious equestrian, and there is a distinct possibility that either he or the mount will be injured.

I would greatly appreciate it if you could find our would-be horse wrangler, and ensure the bodily integrity of both parties. Pray begin your search on the outskirts of Dhoro Iloh─I consider it extremely unlikely he has managed to travel more than a few dozen yalms beyond the Towering Still.
TEXT_BANNAM504_03118_DAILYNAMAZUO03118_0: The Mol make it look so easy. Effortless. I thought I could just leap on its back, and gallop off across the steppe. But, no. No, no, no...
I don't know if I nudged the wrong spot or what, but we were suddenly racing down the side of the cliff! My entire life flashed before my bulging eyes!
Practice makes perfect, or so they say. ...They wouldn't say that if they saw my attempts at riding horses.
I did my best not to nudge the beast the wrong way, but once again I found myself hurtling down the cliffside at a breakneck pace. How fortunate that I have little neck to speak of, let alone break!
It might be best if I retire before I steer myself into a Matanga lair...
Please, would you ride the horse for me? Yes, yes?
A Mol horse handler was to meet me halfway. “Just follow the course of the river to the north,” Seigetsu said. Sounds simple enough, doesn't it...?

Oh, hello. When I saw the horse return alone, I was worried you'd been snagged by one of those long-toothed cats. Well, our Mol friend will be waiting, so it's back in the saddle for you! So to speak.
TEXT_BANNAM504_03118_DAILYMOL03118_000_0: Do those stunted creatures even know how to ride...?
TEXT_BANNAM504_03118_SYSTEM_000_019: Speak with the Namazu horse enthusiast in Nhaama's Retreat to mount a horse, and then deliver the animal to the Mol horse handler.
TEXT_BANNAM504_03118_DAILYMOL03118_000_0: ...You are returning one of our horses? I expected a Namazu rider, but to be honest, I am somewhat relieved.
Hah, did you see it race away!? The poor beast must have been homesick for Mol Iloh!
I thank you for returning our animal in fine health. Pray send my regards to Seigetsu and his kin.
The horse will find its way home, worry not. Feel free to make your own way back to the Namazu.
TEXT_BANNAM504_03118_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: <sigh> As expected, you were forced to salvage my shortsighted─and shortlimbed─kin's duty. I did try to dissuade him from his course...
In any case, my perspicacity in assigning your tasks has been borne out once again.

Unfortunately, however, our enthusiast's zeal is as unrelenting as my intellect, and he is surely doomed to repeat these ill-considered horseback disasters. In such an event, your assistance will once more be welcome.
TEXT_BANNAM505_03119_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Ever since we constructed the mikoshi, we have been expending our supplies of festive paper showers at an alarming rate. I have assigned an official “papermaker” to the task, but as the title was conferred more as a method of encouragement than a recognition of expertise, he may very well be in need of experienced assistance.
If you would, pray locate our papermaker in the vicinity of Kahkol Iloh, and render whatever aid he might require.
TEXT_BANNAM505_03119_DAILYNAMAZUO03119_0: Really? You've come to help me make confetti? Wonderful! We need a massive stockpile─gigantic, even─to cover the needs of our more excitable festival participants.
Do you think you could make me several pairs of scissors? I've sharpened mine so many times there's hardly anything left to sharpen. Look in the crate there, and you should find everything you need.
Do you think you could put together some papermaking frames? I could triple my production! Look in the crate there, and you should find everything you need.
Do you think you could mix up several pots of paste for me? I may have let my last pot dry up... Look in the crate there, and you should find everything you need.
Do you think you could dig into a vein or two of cinnabar for me? Very good for making vermilion pigment. Very red. The locals say the best place to look is to the south of Reunion.
Do you think you could pull up a few tufts of fibrous wildgrass for me? It's the perfect base material for papermaking. You should be able to find some suitable patches to the south of Reunion.

Oh, do you think you could find one of those sparkly dusk scallops for me? I can grind the shells into a splendid pigment for coloring our paper! Seigetsu's books suggested the waters of the lower Yat Khaal, and baiting the hook with salmon roe.
Bring the supplies to me when you're ready, and in the meantime I'll keep soaking and pasting and snipping away!

TEXT_BANNAM505_03119_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: Welcome back, . May I assume that with your intervention, our supplies of confetti have been sufficiently restocked?

...Threw it into the air almost immediately, you say? I have not encountered a word which adequately describes my sense of shame and disappointment. Please say you will stay for a while. We quite obviously need your help.
TEXT_BANNAM506_03120_KOFUINSEIGETSU_000_: , I have a special favor to ask of you. Our altar has frequent need of fresh offerings─fish, fruit, and the like─and we require your assistance in procuring replacements. But these must be no ordinary offerings...
Our head procurer will provide you with the details of your task─you will find him absorbed in his work near the Path of the Craven. ...Oh, and ? Pray keep this request confidential, if you would.
TEXT_BANNAM506_03120_DAILYNAMAZUO03120_0: Seigetsu sent you, yes, yes? Thank the Big One! I need an expert─a veteran in the field─to handle one of the more challenging aspects of the procurement.
To be more specific, I need you to craft a high-quality metal fish sculpture for our altar offerings. As convincingly real as possible! Feel free to raid my supply crate for anything you need.
